architecture: Immutable one-set playback segments with physical boundary ports, per-avatar registration, closed-walk composition, and definition-based persistence with full revalidation on restore.
contracts: Capture the actual ball/hand tracks and accepted elbow interpolation; preparing a different source does not mutate captured motion.
A port includes hand position/orientation, elbow position, both one-sided derivatives, ownership, ball position/derivatives, catch and next-release obligations, cross order and underarm relations.
Compare full ports within 1e-7 numerical roundoff, with a bijection of ball identities; names and near positions alone cannot establish a join.
Use catch events for boundary ownership instead of a floating-point floor selecting a pre-catch sample.
When kinematics already match a registered port, anchor only the new cycle at that elbow path, project onto its IK circles, and validate before registration. Existing segments remain unchanged.
Registration validates the new path at at least 480 samples and at most 3ms spacing, including every exact underarm event, then checks the actual VRM joint motion.
Composition matches every seam including last-to-first, propagates ball permutations, and replays saved segments without invoking the arm path solver.
Closed-walk search uses only registered, matching edges. It does not invent an unverified spatial bridge.

Source append repeats a selected registered interval 1 to 16 times, adds only an existing shortest bridge, preserves the input route and registry, and does not run avatar validation or arm search. The UI previews bridge and return lengths and movement/identity periods; generated transition definitions retain display metadata through save/restore.
Model reload clears registrations. Different ball counts, tempos and radii require a new registry. Changed body settings invalidate captured readers.
Invalid ordinary sequence playback restores an active segment replay. Live pose clearance checks remain enabled.

Persist all source definitions in registration order, including sources that only supplied elbow anchors, mirrors and route references. No imported validation certificate or executable pose is trusted.
Restore rechecks each source on the loaded VRM before publishing the registry. Failed restoration keeps the old registry, preview, playback phase and pause state.
Open and empty routes can be saved as drafts; adjacent boundaries must still match. Playing requires a closed route.
Direct basic-parts and template registration checks motion without replacing the current editor draft or preview.

Requested A/B transitions first search registered edges. Missing transitions try two then four repetitions of each unchanged source plus schedule bridges, validate all new poses, and require both directional port paths before publishing.

For matching Box and opposite-column definitions (Switched, left/right fixed cross and Threaded), a further candidate exchanges column receivers with two 4x throws and holds the short ball. Fixed crosses choose the lower hand first and carry the returning ball above the other arm. Both directions still require full avatar validation and exact registered ports.

Switched/alternating-cross candidates retain column ownership, prepare held routes, use elevated outside short passes during spatial changes, and distinguish the first and second short passes because only the second enters the next stage. Original source cycles and alternating phases remain unchanged.

Five registered round trips connect all six baseline column configurations at 0.205 seconds per beat. All thirty directed source pairs and a six-source closed walk reuse existing segments with the arm planner disabled, in both mirrors.

Register the 56 currently valid height combinations, 18 accepted spatial primitives and 16 basic Double configurations in one registry, connect each to the same base in both directions, then validate thirty closed walks covering all 90 sources with the arm planner disabled, in both mirrors.

Batch preparation stages 90 sources and 89 requested connections behind a private facade, yields before each check with the original preview and registry intact, and publishes only after full base connectivity. Cancel, validation failure, model changes and external registry changes never publish the staged graph. A second batch reuses the same definitions and edges without arm planning. Longer repeated sequences stay registered separately while the two-set source phases required by spatial bridge builders are prepared.

A requested A/B connection may extend an already reachable component through registered C. Generate a supported C/B or A/C bridge only when both directions to C exist; require both requested A/B paths before publishing. Save and restore the exact definitions and intermediate route.

Switched Shuffle retains its overhand release through handoff. Alternating mixed heights retain the correct starting phase; the both-Inverted low-column transition retains crossed elbow preferences through entry and departure.

Box/short-under-catch moves columns one stage before short passes on entry and reverses that order on departure. Explicit bridge coordinates preserve legacy underarm endpoints; event measurements verify the catching point lies beneath the opposite forearm in both mirrors. Source cycles, saved restoration and replay without arm planning remain checked.

Lateral Inverted/Shuffle moves catch height through explicit underhand bridge throws and separates empty hand returns laterally. The original Shuffle retains its claw release and both source cycles retain their flight endpoints and velocities. Both mirrors, restoration and reuse without arm planning pass.

Switched center/cross-side vertical-up lanes temporarily raise the short pass and separate empty returns while retaining vertical flights and column ownership. Both source cycles keep their endpoints and velocities; both mirrors register matching ports.
A candidate graph is forked before generation. Rejected paths leave the registry and preview unchanged. An explicit UI action constructs the A / bridge / B / return route.
Inline transitions insert the existing rank-alignment entry/exit rows while retaining the registry tempo. A valid standalone motion at a different tempo does not imply a valid transition.
A rejected candidate can be explicitly moved into the normal editor with its mirror and failure locations; this does not play or register it.
The UI displays registry ball count and tempo. Optional tempo matching changes and validates only the newly registered definition.

composedExamples.operation: Repeat registered segments; retain the source constraints

browser.reason: Prior local-composer access was rejected by browser URL safety policy. No workaround or new local browser access was attempted.
pending: Register two ordinary cycles with a shared state, inspect compatible next choices, add and undo segments, close and replay the route.
Choose registered motions and repeat counts, inspect append/return previews, undo a complete insertion, toggle transition-only choices and restore their metadata.
Inspect cycle labels, playback controls, failure restoration, model reload, registry clearing and empty states.
Register from parts and templates, save JSON, restore local storage, restore an unfinished route and recover from invalid imports while keeping the preview.
Select source A/B, generate only missing transitions, explicitly create their round trip, and reuse the two existing bridges for a third pair.
Register sources at the displayed tempo, create an In-line transition, import a rejected candidate into the editor, retain mirror/failure locations, and preserve the previous preview.

Register 90 motions including eighteen spatial primitives and sixteen basic Double configurations and choose mixed styles across column types; show an intermediate motion when a new link uses it and reuse completed paths.
Run batch preparation of the basic parts, inspect progress, cancel or recover from failure without changing the registry/route/preview, then prepare again and reuse it without duplicates.
Inspect the anchored elbows and mesh/clothing clearance from front, side and diagonal views.

limitations: The production APIs were exercised headlessly with the real VRM. Live current UI and rendered appearance remain unverified.
A missing port match is not a proof that the human transition is impossible. A new transition must be generated and validated.

Forty-six sources covering the specified basic motion axes register in both mirrors. Standalone distinct cycles have no direct cross-source joins in this inventory. New spatial transitions still require generation or explicit registration.
The automatic generator tries bounded repeated-cycle candidates; it does not construct every possible spatial transition or prove that a failed candidate is impossible.

The 56 currently valid height combinations, eighteen spatial primitives and sixteen basic Double configurations connect to the same base at 0.205 seconds per beat in both mirrors. The other 40 initial height combinations still require spatial adjustment. This does not establish reachability for edited positions, grips or different tempos, or fidelity to the 81 Double entries in the source catalog. In-line entry/exit passes at its baseline beat; the tested 0.16-second candidate is rejected and editable.
Validation is numerical and based on bones and a torso envelope; it is not a proof of continuous mesh clearance or exact source-performance fidelity.
